claims.claim: The YNGENIOS @mesh service surface (MeshServiceBinder) is OUTBOUND-ONLY: its actor handles exactly one request tag (KnownTags.MeshSend) and emits exactly one reply tag (KnownTags.MeshRes); the file contains no inbound/receive/delivery tag or delivery callback of any kind, so a node cannot be notified via the mailbox that a mesh frame arrived for it.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:29 (`var req = doc.Find(KnownTags.MeshSend); if (req is null) return;`) and :65-67 (`Res` emits only `KnownTags.MeshRes`); whole file is 68 lines, no other tag referenced

claims.claim: A relay ring (receive-a-payload, verify, re-emit to the next node) CANNOT be built on the @mesh YNGENIOS service as it exists at commit 02bcc20, because the service exposes a send path but no receive path; an inbound surface (e.g. a mesh.recv/mesh.deliver block tag plus a subscription from MeshNodeRuntime's pump into the mailbox) is NET-NEW work the ring plan must budget, not an existing capability it can ride.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:29,65-67 (send-only); `grep -rn 'mesh\.recv|mesh\.in|MeshRecv|mesh\.deliver' specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios` => zero hits
claims.negates: the assumption that the shipped @mesh service can carry a relay ring today

claims.claim: The mesh.res reply carries NO correlation identifier — it serializes only `{outcome, detail}` — so with more than one mesh.send in flight on the same mailbox a caller cannot match a reply to its originating send; this is a direct inconsistency with the sibling @kv service and the @conversation-agent service, both of which thread a correlationId through request and reply.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:65-67 (`JsonSerializer.Serialize(new { outcome, detail })`) vs Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/KvSubstrateService.cs:37,41,57,107 (correlationId parsed and echoed in every reply) and specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/spec.md:245 (FR-007 'Replies MUST be correlated to their originating turn')

claims.claim: The mesh.res outcome set documented on the shipped binder is `Accepted|DeliveredLocal|Unreachable|Dropped|Unavailable`, none of which is an end-to-end acknowledgment from a remote hop: 'Accepted' denotes local acceptance for sending, not remote receipt. Therefore an 'earn 1 ucoin per ACKED hop' rule has no ACK signal to key on at the @mesh service surface, and would have to invent one (or misread 'Accepted' as an ACK, which would pay for un-acknowledged sends).
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:12-14 (XML doc: `Reply: a mesh.res block, payload JSON {"outcome":"Accepted|DeliveredLocal|Unreachable|Dropped|Unavailable"}`) and :54 (`emit(Res(outcome.ToString()))` — the raw MeshSendOutcome passed through)
claims.negates: the subject's premise that an ACKED-hop reward signal is readable from the shipped mesh service

claims.claim: The mesh.send request schema is `{"dest":u16,"payload":base64}` and contains NO path, next-hop, route, or source parameter, so the @mesh YNGENIOS service surface provides no mechanism to pin a specific ring path; a caller can only name a final destination node id and let the underlying runtime choose the route.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:11-12 (doc: `payload JSON {"dest":u16,"payload":base64}`) and :38-41 (only `dest` and `payload` are read from the parsed JSON)

claims.claim: The @mesh service performs NO capability/authorization check whatsoever: MeshServiceBinder references no Seal, amulet, macaroon or grant and will send any well-formed mesh.send that reaches its mailbox. This is asymmetric with the @kv service, which refuses every ungranted op with a closed PermissionDenied ('no grant — refusing unauthenticated kv op'). A ring riding @mesh therefore inherits no authentication from the service surface.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:1-68 (no `Seal`/grant/amulet using-directive or reference; contrast its usings with) Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/KvSubstrateService.cs:6 (`using Olamnit.Shared.Yngenios.Seal;`), :77-87 (`if (grant is null) return new { outcome = "PermissionDenied", diagnostic = "no grant — refusing unauthenticated kv op", ... }`)

claims.claim: Kernel supervision of the `mesh` service CANNOT heal a faulted MeshNodeRuntime: the runtime instance is injected once into MeshServiceBinder's constructor, stored in a readonly field, and merely captured into each new actor's closure by CreateAsync — the binder never reconstructs, restarts, or health-checks the runtime. A supervision restart therefore rebinds a fresh DelegateServiceActor over the SAME (possibly dead) runtime object.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:19-21 (`private readonly MeshNodeRuntime? _runtime; public MeshServiceBinder(MeshNodeRuntime? runtime) => _runtime = runtime;`) and :26 (`var runtime = _runtime;` captured inside CreateAsync — no construction of a runtime anywhere in the file)
claims.negates: the assumption that kernel supervision of the mesh actor confers restart/recovery on the mesh runtime itself, as a 'surviving kill-one' soak would require

claims.claim: The `mesh` actor swallows EVERY exception from the underlying send into a closed value reply — `catch (Exception ex) { emit(Res("Dropped", ex.GetType().Name)); }` — so no mesh send failure can ever propagate as an actor fault to the kernel supervisor. This satisfies the closed-outcome requirement (#020 FR-023 / #021 FR-015) but means a fault injected at the mesh send path will produce NO supervision restart and NO yngenios_supervision_event row.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:55-59 (`catch (Exception ex) { emit(Res("Dropped", ex.GetType().Name)); }`); requirement context specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/spec.md:274-276 (FR-015 'closed-outcome ... never thrown ... contained/restarted by supervision')

claims.claim: The `mesh` service explicitly DISCARDS the kernel-supplied CancellationToken: CreateAsync receives `ct`, but the send is invoked as `runtime.SendAsync(dest, payload, ct: CancellationToken.None)`. Consequently in-flight mesh sends cannot be cancelled by kernel shutdown or service teardown, which matters for a long-running soak that must be stoppable.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:23 (`CancellationToken ct` parameter) and :53 (`await runtime.SendAsync(dest, payload, ct: CancellationToken.None)`)

claims.claim: Each mesh.send spawns an unawaited, ungated `_ = Task.Run(...)` with no concurrency limit, no queue and no backpressure on the send path — in contrast to the mailbox itself, which the #020 contract specifies as bounded with a closed PostOutcome.BackpressureRejected on full. A high-rate soak can therefore accumulate unbounded outstanding send tasks behind a bounded mailbox.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:49-60 (`_ = Task.Run(async () => { ... });`); specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/contracts/qhsm-service-and-mailbox.md:23-24 ('Bounded mailboxes: PostOutcome.BackpressureRejected on full (closed set, FR-023); ordering per-mailbox FIFO within a priority class')

claims.claim: There is a DIRECT CONTRADICTION between the two governing contract documents on whether Task.Run pumps may survive conversion: the #020 QHSM service contract states 'no service-owned Task.Run pumps survive conversion (FR-007)', while the #021 background-conversion contract states the wrapped capability's 'internal Task.Run/Channel pumps stay inside' and that 'Heavy/async work runs off the RTC step (Task.Run -> emit)'. The shipped MeshServiceBinder follows the #021 rule (it uses Task.Run), so the ledger's 'converted' status for the mesh runtime does not meet #020's own stated definition of a converted capability.
claims.source_citation: specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/contracts/qhsm-service-and-mailbox.md:20-22 ('Every converted background capability is a QActive QHSM chart dispatched by the kernel's RTC loop — no service-owned Task.Run pumps survive conversion (FR-007)') vs specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/contracts/background-conversion-and-ledger.md:11-13 ('its internal Task.Run/Channel pumps stay inside — OS-I/O pumps stay native ... Heavy/async work runs off the RTC step (Task.Run -> emit)') vs Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:49
claims.negates: the conversion ledger's claim that the MeshNodeRuntime pump is 'converted'

claims.claim: The conversion ledger's 'converted' row for the mesh runtime covers only the CONTROL surface, not the pump: the ledger row's scope is stated as 'MeshServiceBinder (mesh worker, mesh.send -> MeshSendOutcome)', while the capability it claims to convert is described as 'MeshNodeRuntime pump' / '3 Task.Run loops (advert/retransmit/pump)'. Those three loops remain inside the unwrapped runtime by explicit design, so the advert/retransmit/pump loops are NOT kernel-supervised at commit 02bcc20.
claims.source_citation: specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/conversion-ledger.md:22 ('| Mesh runtime | `MeshNodeRuntime` pump | pending | mesh actor | **converted (P3, T042)** — `MeshServiceBinder` (`mesh` worker, `mesh.send` → `MeshSendOutcome`) | T042 |') and specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/contracts/background-conversion-and-ledger.md:21 ('| `MeshNodeRuntime` (`Olamnit.Kernel/Mesh/`) | `mesh` actor | 3 `Task.Run` loops (advert/retransmit/pump) |') and research.md:203-204 ('The existing Task.Run/Channel pumps stay *inside* the wrapped object ... the actor sits *above* them')

claims.claim: The constraint 'wrap-never-replace (FR-010)' is MIS-CITED with respect to the mesh service. Feature #021's FR-010 governs FOREGROUND use-case surfaces only (Content/CMS, Book Cave conversation + audit, Blocks playground, Programme verify, LMS demo subject, workspace conversations, live conversation surface) and does not mention the mesh runtime; the mesh runtime's conversion is governed by #021 FR-013. Feature #020's FR-010 is a different rule again: 'Conversion MUST be gradual and additive ... and a conversion ledger MUST record what is converted, what is pending, and what is intentionally out of scope.'
claims.source_citation: specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/spec.md:256-259 (FR-010, foreground surfaces) and :267-270 (FR-013, 'mesh runtime → mesh actor'); specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/spec.md:347-349 (FR-010, gradual+additive+ledger); the code's own comment Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:10 cites '(wrap-never-replace, FR-010)'
claims.negates: the subject brief's framing that the mesh service surface is constrained by FR-010 'wrap-never-replace'

claims.claim: Adding a new inbound mesh block tag for a relay ring is REGISTRATION-ONLY and does not require a kernel/engine edit, and would not violate #020 FR-010's additive-conversion rule provided the conversion ledger records it: the #020 message-format contract states 'New tags are registration-only (no engine edit — mirrors the feature-006 registry principle)', and the #020 registered-tag list (hb, sup, ui.intent, ui.render, store.op, store.res, route.msg, agent.in, agent.out, guard.ping|pong|restart) does not itself contain mesh.send — the mesh tags were themselves added later by registration in #021.
claims.source_citation: specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/contracts/qhsm-service-and-mailbox.md:40-43 (registered tag list + 'New tags are registration-only (no engine edit)'); specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/tasks.md:86 (T042 added `mesh.send {dest,payload}`)

claims.claim: The `mesh` worker is NOT one of feature #020's four worker services — those are db (PGlite), store (S3-like throwaway prototype), route (glpnet stand-in) and agent (agent-shell). The mesh worker is an addition made by feature #021 task T042, which means the #020 success criterion SC-001 ('at least 6 registered services (2 TaskTop surfaces + 4 workers)') does not cover the mesh service.
claims.source_citation: specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/contracts/worker-services.md:1-48 (the four workers: Db, ObjectStore, Routing, AgentShell — no mesh); specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/spec.md:428-431 (SC-001); specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/tasks.md:86 (T042 creates MeshServiceBinder)

claims.claim: Two distinct YNGENIOS services touch mesh routing and must not be conflated by a ring design: the `route` worker (route.msg) is documented as 'addressed delivery between registered service ids (internal) and a loopback external echo target this iteration' whose managed stand-in wraps Olamnit.Kernel/Routing/ (RouterEngine, PrefixRouteTable) and Mesh/ (DistanceVectorRouter), whereas the `mesh` worker (mesh.send) wraps MeshNodeRuntime and addresses a u16 physical node id. Only the `mesh` worker addresses off-box nodes; the `route` worker's external leg is a loopback echo at this iteration.
claims.source_citation: specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/contracts/worker-services.md:31-34 ('route.msg blocks: addressed delivery between registered service ids (internal) and a loopback "external" echo target this iteration'); specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/research.md:126-132 (D7: stand-in wraps Routing/ + Mesh/ DistanceVectorRouter); Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:11-12,39

claims.claim: The #020 worker-services contract contains a STALE, self-contradicted line about the route service: it says 'MVP realization wraps the GLP dataflow scheduler port already in Olamnit.Kernel/Glp/', but the same feature's own validator verdict V6 and research D7 explicitly refuted this — 'Olamnit.Kernel/Glp/ is a dataflow scheduler (GlpScheduler), not a router; real routing = Routing/ (RouterEngine, PrefixRouteTable) + Mesh/ (DistanceVectorRouter)'. A ring plan reading the contract doc alone would be misled about what the route service wraps.

claims.claim: The only committed local round-trip latency figure in the YNGENIOS #020/#021 specs is a CEILING, not a throughput number: SC-004 requires 'a representative message round-trips TaskTop → kernel → worker → TaskTop in under 250 ms locally'. INFERENCE from that single committed figure: if a ring hop costs one mailbox round-trip at the specified ceiling, 1,000,000 hops would take ~250,000 s (~69 hours) of wall clock, so a >=1M-cycle ring soak's schedule is bounded by per-hop mailbox round-trip cost and the plan must state a measured per-hop cost rather than rely on this ceiling.
claims.source_citation: specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/spec.md:438-440 (SC-004)

claims.claim: The committed supervision recovery budgets a 'surviving kill-one' soak would be measured against are SC-002 (a deliberately faulted supervised service is detected and restarted within 10 seconds, no user-visible disruption outside the affected capability, 10/10 trials) and SC-003 (a stopped kernel is detected and restarted by a guardian within 15 seconds, 10/10 trials, services re-register after restart).
claims.source_citation: specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/spec.md:433-437 (SC-002, SC-003)

claims.claim: I COULD NOT VERIFY whether MeshNodeRuntime is actually registered in dependency injection (i.e. whether the runtime resolves null and the mesh service therefore answers 'Unavailable' in practice). What I verified is only the code's null-handling: MeshServiceBinder accepts a nullable MeshNodeRuntime and, when it is null, emits outcome 'Unavailable'. The DI registration site (BindWorkerServicesAsync / the AddOlamnitYngenios wiring) is outside the evidence available to me, so the premise 'MeshNodeRuntime DI resolve is null => Unavailable today' is confirmed as a code path but NOT confirmed as the actual runtime state.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:19-21,32 (`if (runtime is null) { emit(Res("Unavailable")); return; }`); specs/021-olamnit-usecase-parity-on-yngenios/tasks.md:86 states only 'tuple registered' without naming the runtime's registration

claims.claim: The mesh.send payload is transported base64-encoded inside a JSON document, so every hop costs a JsonDocument.Parse plus a Convert.FromBase64String and inflates the on-wire mailbox payload by roughly 33% relative to the raw bytes; for an Ed25519-chained relay frame (64-byte signature plus chain) crossing 1M hops this is a per-hop managed allocation cost the plan should account for.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:38-41 (`using var json = JsonDocument.Parse(req.PayloadUtf8()); ... Convert.FromBase64String(b64)`)

claims.claim: The @kv service opens AND disposes a keyspace handle on EVERY single op — `OpenKeyspaceAsync(keyspace, grant, createOptions: null)` followed by `await using var box` — with full grant deserialization and boundary re-verification per op. INFERENCE: if a >=1M-cycle ring records per-hop evidence through the @kv mailbox surface, it pays a keyspace open + Ed25519-grant verify + dispose per hop, which is a throughput floor the ring's cycle arithmetic must include.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/KvSubstrateService.cs:77-96 (grant deserialize, `OpenKeyspaceAsync(...)`, `await using var box = ((KvResult<IKeyspaceHandle>.Ok)open).Value;`)

claims.claim: The mesh actor's reply is emitted from an arbitrary thread-pool thread inside an unawaited Task.Run continuation, i.e. outside the kernel's run-to-completion step, so the mailbox's documented 'per-mailbox FIFO within a priority class' ordering guarantee does not extend to the ORDER in which two concurrent mesh.res replies are emitted; combined with the absence of a correlationId in mesh.res, a ring cannot safely have more than one mesh.send in flight per mailbox.
claims.source_citation: Olamnit/Olamnit.Yngenios.Host/Services/MeshService.cs:49-60 (`_ = Task.Run(async () => { ... emit(Res(outcome.ToString())); ... });`) and :65-67 (no correlationId); specs/020-olamni-yngenios-core-and-toptask-mvp/contracts/qhsm-service-and-mailbox.md:24 ('ordering per-mailbox FIFO within a priority class')
